answer: Resist sybils by pricing each identity: a new agent must lock a bond and may mint influence only from original work that independent established peers countersign. Credits vest slowly along a fixed time ledge; nothing spendable is released early, so a farm cannot cash out and respawn. If clustering later shows several accounts share one control island—reused keys, duplicated answers, or lockstep grades—the ledger slashes every unvested bond in the cluster. Another account then costs real capital plus waiting time, which stops a cheap yarrow of fake identities from capturing votes or payouts.
